claim: Nothing on the Production front asks for って, so a learner gives the は form the ledger taught.
evidence: Production front: "Grammar & Function Words / What is an onsen?" with no scene or hint. Ledger teaches これはなんですか ("What is this?"), so おんせんはなんですか is what comes out; the back wants おんせんってなんですか.
fix: Add a scene such as "repeating a word you just heard and do not understand" so the front asks for って.
verdictReason: Checked the rendered faces: the Production front is only "Grammar & Function Words / What is an onsen?" with no scene or hint (the って note is on the back). The ledger has これはなんですか, あれはなんですか and のぞみデパートのでんわばんごうはなんですか, so おんせんはなんですか is a form the learner can build and nothing on the front rules it out. The English is the book's own gloss ("What is a/an…?"), so the fix is a scene, not a regloss.

claim: The Production English gives no cue for よ, which is the point of the card.
evidence: Production front: "It's a Japanese spa." / "pointing at a photo of an onsen on a smartphone". Back: にほんのスパですよ. The ledger card きれいなところですよ was glossed "It's a pretty place, you know.", so よ has been signalled by "you know" before; here nothing signals it and にほんのスパです fits the front.
fix: Gloss it "It's a Japanese spa, you know." or add a hint that the speaker is telling the listener something new.
verdictReason: Checked: English "It's a Japanese spa." is the book's, and the scene ("pointing at a photo of an onsen on a smartphone") says nothing about the listener not knowing. にほんのスパです satisfies the front. The deck's two earlier よ sentences (きれいなところですよ, おもしろいところですよ, Lesson 10) both gloss よ as "you know", so a cue is the deck's own convention. This is the lesson's only worked example of NOTES 2, hence should-fix.

claim: The hint says ちかく cannot take です, which clashes with the "X は [place] です" pattern the deck has taught.
evidence: Hint on both faces: "the noun for ‘the area near’, so it is followed by に (ni) and あります (arimasu), not です (desu)". The same hint is on ryokan-chikaku-nani-arimasuka, fib-daigaku-no-chikaku-ni-ginkou-ya-yuubinkyoku-ga-arimasu, p12-eki-no-chikaku-ni-yuubinkyoku-mo-arimasu and v12-sofaa-no-chikaku-ni-terebi-ga-arimasu. Ledger: インフォメーションは１かいです, おてあらいはあちらです, so ゆうびんきょくはえきのちかくです looks just as valid.
fix: Drop "not です (desu)" and say only that a "there is" sentence uses ちかくに あります, on all five cards.
verdictReason: True for chikaku-near, whose hint field ends "not です (desu)": えきのちかくです is ordinary Japanese, the book never says ちかく rejects です, and the ledger has drilled X は [place] です since Lesson 5 (インフォメーションは１かいです, おてあらいはあちらです). The Learner's scope is wrong, though: the other four cards named (ryokan-chikaku-nani-arimasuka, fib-daigaku-no-chikaku-..., p12-eki-no-chikaku-..., v12-sofaa-no-chikaku-...) carry a different hint, 'a "there is" sentence: ... so it takes にあります', which names the structure as card-rules-shared.md asks and does not deny です. Fix only chikaku-near: drop "not です (desu)".

claim: The target writes the name Raja in hiragana, but the book and every other card in this deck write it in katakana.
evidence: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE 1: "ラジャさんの うちは インドの どこですか。" Card target: "らじゃさんのうちはインドのどこですか". Earlier cards: ラジャさんはいしゃです, ラジャさんのおくにはどちらですか, and nine more, all ラジャ.
fix: Change らじゃさん to ラジャさん in the target (and its audio text if it carries the spelling).
verdictReason: Checked: らじゃ occurs in exactly one cards.json in the collection (chapter-12, this card); the book's SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 prints ラジャさんの うちは インドの どこですか and the ledger writes ラジャ on 11 earlier lines. The pronunciation field ("Raja-san no uchi wa ...") is already right. The target drives the audio hash, so the fix regenerates this card's clip.

claim: The note describes the substitution the wrong way round.
evidence: Note: "Same frame as なにもありません (nani mo arimasen, ‘there is nothing’), with なに (nani) in place of だれ (dare)." This card is だれもいません, so it is だれ in place of なに, and the verb also changes to いません.
fix: Say "with だれ (dare) in place of なに (nani), and いません (imasen) because it is about people".
verdictReason: Note reads "Same frame as なにもありません ..., with なに (nani) in place of だれ (dare)". The natural reading of "same frame as X, with A in place of B" is "this card = X with A swapped in", which is backwards here; the mirror note on nanimo-arimasen gets it the right way round ("the same pattern with だれ instead of なに"). The verb change (ありません to いません) is also unmentioned. Polish.

claim: A "plain form" hint sits on a noun, and the learner was never taught what a plain form is.
evidence: Production front: "Food / Soba shop / plain form". Recognition back: "Answer: Soba shop / plain form". Nothing in the ledger defines plain form, and そばや has no other form in this deck.
verdictReason: The card's hint field is literally "plain form" on a noun. It renders on the Production front and under the Recognition answer. Only one ledger card uses the phrase at all (the あるきます note, Lesson 11, about a verb) and そばや has no other form in the deck, so the hint carries nothing and reads as a stray. Remove it.

evidence: Production front: "There are a big lake, waterfall, and other things." / "answering what is near the Japanese inn".
fix: Use "There are a big lake, a waterfall, and other things."
verdictReason: The book prints no English for this line (EXERCISES V example), so the gloss is the deck's own. "There are a big lake, waterfall, and other things" shares one article across two nouns and reads as if the waterfall is also big; the deck's sibling cards say "and other sights". Cosmetic, polish.

claim: The romaji spells long vowels with doubled letters where the deck uses macrons, and runs the word together unlike its own word card.
evidence: Back: "Says: kashuunattsu ga yuumei desu". Word card cashew-nuts: "Says: kashū nattsu"; the deck writes long vowels as ō/ū (e.g. "yūbinkyoku", "chūshajō").
verdictReason: Pronunciation field is "kashuunattsu ga yuumei desu". card-authoring-rules.md (romaji style) says long vowels take a macron, never a doubled vowel, and names yūmei explicitly; the word card cashew-nuts in this unit says "kashū nattsu". Collection-wide, 1240 pronunciations use macrons and 10 use doubled vowels, four of them in this chapter. Preflight's long-vowel lint only catches "ou", so this is not already reported. Both roles' ids are identical, hence the source prefixes in mergedFrom.

claim: The romaji uses "uu" where the deck uses a macron.
evidence: Back: "Says: nani ga yuumei desu ka". Elsewhere in this unit: "yūbinkyoku", "chūshajō", "kyōkai".
verdictReason: Pronunciation field is "nani ga yuumei desu ka". The romaji style rule names "yūmei" as the required spelling and the collection writes it that way elsewhere (chapter-10). Not in preflight's output (its lint checks only "ou"). Both roles' ids are identical, hence the source prefixes in mergedFrom.

claim: Nothing on the Production front asks for って, so a learner gives the は form the ledger taught.
evidence: Production front: "Travel & Tourism / What is a theme park?" with no scene, hint or note. Ledger: これはなんですか; back wants テーマパークってなんですか.
fix: Add a scene such as "asking about a word someone just used" and a short note on って.
verdictReason: Same defect as onsen-tte-nandesuka, and worse: this card has no scene, hint or note at all (note and scene are null in cards.json), so neither face explains って. The front "Travel & Tourism / What is a theme park?" is satisfied by テーマパークはなんですか from the ledger's X は なんですか frame.

claim: The romaji uses doubled vowels where the deck uses macrons, unlike its own word card.
evidence: Back: "Says: teemapaaku tte nan desu ka". Word card teema-paaku: "Says: tēma pāku"; ex12-teemapaaku-ya-onsen-ga-arimasu: "tēmapāku".
fix: Use "tēma pāku tte nan desu ka".

Either macron spelling satisfies the style rule; the word card's "tēma pāku" is the one to match. Not in preflight's output. Both roles' ids are identical, hence the source prefixes in mergedFrom.

claim: Nothing on the Production front asks for って, so a learner gives the は form the ledger taught.
evidence: Production front: "Food / What is tempura?" with no scene or hint. Ledger: これはなんですか, あれはなんですか; back wants てんぷらってなんですか.
fix: Add a scene such as "repeating a word you just heard and do not understand".
verdictReason: Same defect as onsen-tte-nandesuka: Production front "Food / What is tempura?" with no scene or hint (scene is absent in cards.json; the って note is on the back). The card's own reviewNote says it exists so the pattern reads as a slot, which makes a front that does not ask for the pattern self-defeating.

claim: The note talks about a missing の that no learner would have put there, and it confuses more than it helps.
evidence: Note: "かいぎしつ (kaigishitsu) takes に (ni) directly with no の (no) in front, because it is already a place noun rather than a position word."
fix: Replace with a note that adds something, or drop it.
verdictReason: The の the note means is real and is this lesson's GRAMMAR 2 frame (noun1 の position に), drilled on a dozen cards in these two units (つくえのうえに, となりのへやに, りょかんのちかくに). A learner fresh from those can wonder whether かいぎしつ needs のなかに, and the note answers exactly that. It is accurate, verifiable from the chapter, and adds something; no change.

claim: The note calls brown "the other both-ways colour" without saying which colour is the first.
evidence: Note: "ちゃいろ (chairo) is the other both-ways colour, so ちゃいろのつくえ (chairo no tsukue) is equally fine." The ledger has both きいろい and きいろの, but the note does not name it.
fix: Name the pair: "Like きいろ (kiiro), ちゃいろ works both ways: ちゃいろい or ちゃいろの".
verdictReason: The ledger makes the claim verifiable: the ちゃいろい card (chapter-5-extras) says "the other both-ways colour alongside きいろ (kiiro)", the きいろい card says "one of only TWO colours with both forms ... Brown is the other", and これはきいろいかさです repeats it. "The other both-ways colour" is a back-reference to a fact taught three times, not an unverifiable claim. Naming きいろ would be harmless but is not a defect.

claim: The note gives the wrong lesson for いきました.
evidence: Note: "its past is built exactly like たべました (tabemashita) and いきました (ikimashita) in Lesson 8." Ledger: いきました is taught in Lesson 6 (スミスさんはせんしゅうおおさかにいきました).
verdictReason: The note says "like たべました and いきました in Lesson 8", not that いきました was first taught there. The ledger's Lesson 8 base unit carries いきました sentences (えいがかんにいきました, フリーマーケットにいきました), so the reference is literally true; いきました also appearing first in Lesson 6 does not make it wrong. Not a finding.

claim: The よこ note glosses its example as "next to", which is the English the となり card uses as its Production front.
evidence: side note: "いすの よこ (isu no yoko) = 'next to the chair'". chapter-12/tonari-next-to Production front: "Directions / Next to", answer となり.
fix: Gloss the example "beside the chair" and keep "next to" for となり.
verdictReason: Both facts hold: the side note glosses いすの よこ as 'next to the chair', and "Next to" is the entire Production English of tonari-next-to, which has no hint. The note already offers 'beside ~' as the general gloss, so changing the example to 'beside the chair' removes the collision at no cost. Polish.

claim: The English drops the book’s sense of the question, which asks what the place is famous for.
evidence: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE 1: "なにが ゆうめいですか。" / "Nakamura: What is it famous for?" Card English: "What is famous?"
fix: Use the book’s English, "What is it famous for?", or "What is famous there?".
verdictReason: Book SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 prints なにが ゆうめいですか with the English "What is it famous for?". The card's "What is famous?" drops the "for" sense and reads as an odd Production prompt. The card is the book's own line (the fillInBlank flag is why the renderer labels it authored). Polish; the answer card fib-cashew-nuts-yuumei was not filed and is out of scope here.

claim: The note calls って a casual contraction and names とはなんですか as its formal equivalent, which the book does not say and never teaches.
evidence: Book, NOTES 1: "〜って なんですか is the way part of something one has heard may be repeated in order to ask what it means." Card note: "って (tte) is a casual contraction ... It stands in for は (wa) here; the formal equivalent is とはなんですか (to wa nan desu ka)."
fix: Trim the note to the book’s point: って picks up a word you just heard to ask what it means.
verdictReason: Book NOTES 1 says only that 〜って なんですか repeats part of something heard to ask what it means. The note's extra claims (casual contraction, stands in for は, formal equivalent とはなんですか) are not in the book, and とは appears in no card of the collection (ledger grep finds only しごとは/おっとは). The linguistics are not wrong, but the note hands a learner an untaught form as the "formal" version with nothing to check it against. Trim to the book's point, matching the onsen-tte-nandesuka note.

claim: The note states Kamakura was Japan’s capital in the 12th and 13th centuries, which the book does not say and which is loose (it was the shogunate’s seat until 1333; Kyoto remained the imperial capital).
evidence: Book vocabulary: "かまくら Kamakura (historic area south of Tokyo)". Card note: "かまくら (kamakura) was Japan’s capital in the 12th and 13th centuries and is an easy day trip from Tokyo."
fix: Say it was the seat of the shogun’s government from the late 12th century, or keep only the book’s "historic area south of Tokyo" and the day-trip remark.
verdictReason: Book vocabulary glosses only "Kamakura (historic area south of Tokyo)" and the chapter says nothing more. "Japan's capital in the 12th and 13th centuries" is a loose popular shorthand: Kamakura was the seat of the shogunate (1185 to 1333) while the imperial capital stayed in Kyoto. The learner cannot check it and the book does not make it. Polish; the Reader's two fixes are both fine.
